journal.extremedimensions.tethered.title: 1. Tethered
journal.extremedimensions.tethered.text: If you can read this, you are still held. Good. Most who find this book are not. There is a cord older than the mountains, woven through every living thing in this world. We called it the Tether. It does not speak. It does not need to. The Tether knows. Before you step through any wound, find a stone that remembers north.
journal.extremedimensions.anchor.title: 2. The Anchor
journal.extremedimensions.anchor.text: A stone that remembers north: chiseled stone, eight times, around a single diamond. The lodestone drinks what you give it and turns warm, like a hand. Coal, and the rods the breezes leave behind, for the burning place. Pearls and echoes for the pale one. Set it close to the wound, never far. An anchor too far from the wound is only a stone, and stones do not keep anyone alive.
journal.extremedimensions.cord.title: 3. The Cord
journal.extremedimensions.cord.text: Feeding the anchor is not enough. You must bind yourself to it. A length of iron chain, bound with two cords of string. Wrap it around the anchor and carry the other end through the wound. On this side the cord is short: five strides from the anchor and it snaps. Walk straight into the wound. Down there it trails behind you over the ground, and every step away from the wound pulls it tighter. Walk far and they drink faster. Tear a new wound closer to where you must go.
journal.extremedimensions.wound.title: 4. Wounds
journal.extremedimensions.wound.text: A portal is not a door. Doors are built. Portals are torn. Stand close and you will feel it pulling at the edges of you, the way a wound pulls at stitches. When the path between anchor and wound is blocked, the anchor bleeds into nothing. Keep the way open.
journal.extremedimensions.ember_deep.tex: Below the fire there is a heat that is not fire. The pigmen trade in gold and will not tell you why. I believe they are paying someone. Every breath down there costs warmth, and the anchor pays it for you. Count the seconds. They are counting too.
journal.extremedimensions.pale_void.text: There is no ground in the pale place, only islands that pretend. The tall ones watch you with too much interest. They do not attack because you look at them. They attack because you remind them. Of what, I did not want to know.
journal.extremedimensions.starved.title: 7. The Starved
journal.extremedimensions.starved.text: They are not demons. They were never demons. They are what is left when a soul stays too long where it was not anchored. Hungry for warmth they no longer make. When your anchor runs dry, they do not kill you. They drink. Killing is just what is left.
journal.extremedimensions.ended.title: 8. Ended
journal.extremedimensions.ended.text: I lost a companion beyond the wound today. Not to the hunger. To an ordinary blade. His anchor went cold the moment he fell, as if it had only ever been holding him. The Tether pulled him home empty. He woke in the grass and did not remember my name for an hour.
journal.extremedimensions.scars.title: 9. What They Keep
journal.extremedimensions.scars.text: Every return costs something. A little strength. A little warmth. A little of your name. The marks do not fade. They stay, and they gather, and every one makes room for the next. I think the Tether wants us to earn our wholeness back, piece by piece: by walking where they can see us, by coming home, by surviving the dark. And every death undoes half of what was earned.
journal.extremedimensions.fragment.title: 10. A Fragment
journal.extremedimensions.fragment.text: It fell from one of them, glowing the colour of soul fire. It hums against the anchor. It is a piece of the cord itself, frayed loose. Offered to an anchor, it mends. What it mends, and with whose soul, I prefer not to ask.
journal.extremedimensions.mending.title: 11. Mending
journal.extremedimensions.mending.text: I gave the fragment to the anchor and a mark on my soul closed like an eye. Somewhere, I am sure of it, someone else's opened. The Tether does not create. It only moves things.
journal.extremedimensions.weavers.title: 12. The Weavers
journal.extremedimensions.weavers.text: Deep under everything there are cities of black stone, built by hands that did not need light. In their center stands a great frame, and nothing in it. They did not build a portal. They tried to close one. They used the only thread strong enough. Themselves.
journal.extremedimensions.unanchored.tex: It dropped a pearl when it died, and in the pearl I saw a field of grass. Endermen carry blocks. They cannot bear water. They scream when you meet their eyes. I used to think they were thieves. Now I think they are trying to build something. An anchor. A way home.
journal.extremedimensions.habit.title: 14. Habit
journal.extremedimensions.habit.text: Five times through the wound and back. It gets easier, and that is the danger. The Tether held. It always holds. But I have started to feel it tighten when I leave, like it is reminding me who it belongs to.
journal.extremedimensions.silence.title: 15. Silence
journal.extremedimensions.silence.text: I asked the Tether what it wants. It did not answer. It never answers. But my anchor flared, and for a moment I heard a thousand voices hold their breath. Keep your anchors full. Not for you. For them.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.1: Every portal is a wound. Every wound remembers.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.2: They did not die. They were woven.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.3: Feed the anchor, or they will feed on you.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.5: Gold does not buy mercy. Only time.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.6: Do not linger where the dead are hungry.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.7: Something guards the silence of the Weavers.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.8: Hold fast. Let go, and you are theirs.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.9: The tall ones were travelers once.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.10: Count the seconds. They are counting too.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.11: It does not speak. It does not need to.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.12: Older than the mountains. Hungrier than the void.
menu.extremedimensions.quote.13: An anchor too far from the wound is only a stone.

journal.extremedimensions.tribe.title: 16. The Tribe
journal.extremedimensions.tribe.text: I am not the first to walk between the wounds. There was a tribe before us, long forgotten, that learned to live in the seams. They did not die. They thinned. Now they stand at the edge of the trees, on the ridge, on the far bank of the lava, and watch. Not all of them stand in the open. Some went down into the dark under the stone, and some went lower still, to the cities that were old before we came. It sees. It waits. It takes. Never meet its eyes for long. Never let it near your anchors. And if it comes closer while you are not looking, know that it does not hate you. It only wants what is yours.

journal.extremedimensions.soul_light.tex: I watched one drink. It held the light of my anchor like water in cupped hands, and I could do nothing. Then the wind turned, and the soul lantern by the gate flared blue, and it flinched. They will not drink where souls burn. Hang a soul lantern near your anchors. Light a soul campfire. It does not keep them away. It only keeps them thirsty.
journal.extremedimensions.ruined_gate.te: The broken portals in the wilds are not ruins. They are graves. Each was a wound someone opened without an anchor, and each one closed on them. I found a chain in the obsidian of one, still warm. I did not follow where it led.
journal.extremedimensions.first_wound.te: The tribe did not find the seams. They made them. The first wound was a door, cut so they could walk where nothing could follow. But a door works both ways, and something hungry came through, and they ran into the seams to hide. They have been hiding ever since. Watching. Waiting for it to forget them.

journal.extremedimensions.hollows.title: 20. The Hollows
journal.extremedimensions.hollows.text: I followed one. It ran, my compass clutched to its chest, and it did not vanish until it reached a hollow under the dark oaks: a barrel, bones, webs, candles nobody lights, and everything I had ever lost. They do not want our things. They want to remember what having things was like. A hoard whispers. Follow the ink in the air.
journal.extremedimensions.little_thieves: The hoards have children. Small, quick, grey as ash, and they giggle. They freeze when you look at them, like a game. Look away and your torches are gone. They are frightened of everything except soul light, and they love what the Tether leaves behind. I gave one a fragment by a soul lantern, and it has not left my side since.
journal.extremedimensions.keeper.title: 22. The Keeper
journal.extremedimensions.keeper.text: Every hoard has a keeper: older than the others, its mask bleached like bone. It does not watch. It does not wait. Touch what it guards and it comes, roaring, through the trees. Fight it near the hoard or run far. It will not follow you beyond what it keeps.

journal.extremedimensions.seam.title: 23. The Seam
journal.extremedimensions.seam.text: Between the wounds there is a place that is not a place. Islands of quiet stone hang in nothing, and the light comes from everywhere and nowhere. I stepped out of a gate of pale stone, and the rift I came through hangs between its pylons. It does not stay where I left it: it drifts, slowly, like a boat on a still lake, back and forth over the threshold. When the mist hides the gate, I look for the gold. No other light here is that colour. My chain is the only thing that knows the way back. Do not let go of it.
journal.extremedimensions.loom.title: 24. The Loom
journal.extremedimensions.loom.text: The Weavers were here. Their looms still stand: pillars of hush stone strung with silk as thick as rope, stretched between islands. The silk is warm. It hums when I touch it. I think they wove the Tether here, before anyone needed one.
journal.extremedimensions.thinned.title: 25. The Thinned
journal.extremedimensions.thinned.text: I found their village. Low houses, cold hearths, and graves: mounds of hush stone with a skull and a candle on each. The Lurkers that walk here do not steal. They only watch me, the way you watch a guest who arrived too late. This was their home before they had to hide in ours.

journal.extremedimensions.woven.title: 26. Woven
journal.extremedimensions.woven.text: Iron holds, but iron does not forgive. Silk does. I wove the Seam's thread through my chain by soul light, and the hunger behind me slowed, as if it could not quite find me. The Weavers' own weave goes further: when the charge runs dry, it comes apart thread by thread and carries you home instead. And every mark I endure to the end leaves a scar. Scars are harder to drink from.

journal.extremedimensions.seal.title: 27. The Seal
journal.extremedimensions.seal.text: The dragon was never the enemy. It was the lock. It coiled around the first wound like a scar around a cut, and we killed it for its egg and its breath. I felt the world crack when it fell. The tribe felt it too: they do not take any more. They leave things at the edges of our camps, like offerings to something they hope will protect them. Every rift now opens near the Heart of the Seam. Something there is waking.
journal.extremedimensions.storms.title: 28. Wound Storms
journal.extremedimensions.storms.text: The sky tore above the fields today. Not lightning: a seam, opening and closing like a mouth. Darkness rolled out of it, my anchors guttered, and things from the burning place and the pale one fell through and stood up in the grass. It lasted a minute. It will happen again, until someone mends what was broken.
journal.extremedimensions.heart.title: 29. The Heart
journal.extremedimensions.heart.text: Where all the threads meet, there is an altar of silk, and four great pillars stand round it on islands of their own. When I stood on the altar it rose out of the stone: starved to the bone, hooded, nothing in the hood but a mouth of embers, a crown of broken iron on its brow, its ribs open on a belly of fire that is always empty. It is no Weaver; it is the hunger that came through. It flies. It calls the young of the tribe, red-eyed, and the rays turn on you. It bites through the thread that leads you home, and drags you close when it is dying. But feed the pillars silk, enough of them at once, and their light chains it down. And the Thinned fight beside those who were kind to their young.
journal.extremedimensions.wanderer.title: 30. The Wanderer
journal.extremedimensions.wanderer.text: You have been reading my journal all this time and never asked who wrote it. I was the first to bind a tether, and the first to walk the seams, and the last of the tribe who did not thin. I wrote this for whoever came after, because someone always does. Now it is yours to finish. Mend it, and the world forgets the wound. Sever it, and the world forgets the Tether. I could never choose. You must.
journal.extremedimensions.ending.title: 31. The Ending
journal.extremedimensions.ending.text: It is done. Whatever was chosen, it was chosen for all of us. If it was mended: the storms are gone, the tribe brings gifts instead of taking, and the wounds bleed slower. If it was severed: the Tether no longer counts our seconds beyond the wound, but whoever falls there loses everything they carried, forever. Either way, the journal ends here. The story does not. Six threads are still to be woven on a Weaver's Loom, and the world is not finished until the last of them holds.

viewer.extremedimensions.barter.gift.des: Give it to a Hollowling: it carries it home, and the tribe thinks better of you.
viewer.extremedimensions.spindle.desc: Load the fragments and the silk with a use, then turn it with an empty hand.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.tether_fra: Found in the Fray's tangles, in the Seam's looms, reliquaries and barrels, in the tribe's hoards and the Held's remains; Keepers, Elders and the larger creatures leave it, and a Hollowling sells one every day. Offer it at an anchor to atone for a tenth of what a curse still asks (five at most for each stack), or spin it into Tether Cord.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.wanderers_: Found in the Seam's looms, reliquaries and barrels, in the Fray's tangles and in the tribe's hoards; Keepers leave them, Lurkers leave them as offerings and a befriended Hollowling brings them. Use one to add it to your Tether Journal.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.loose_leaf: Lies in the Held's chamber, at the end of a warm chain. Use it to read it into your Tether Journal; it is not used up.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.seam_silk: Found in the Seam's looms, reliquaries and barrels and in the Fray's tangles; Seam Veins give it when broken, and the Thinned, Cragbacks, Edgecrawlers, Frayed Rays and the Knot Mother leave it.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.tether_cor: Spun on a Spindle from Tether Fragments and Seam Silk; now and then in the Fray's tangles and the Seam's reliquaries. It binds Tetherite Scrap into an ingot, and held in the other hand at a smithing table it steadies a binding.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.tetherite_: Smelted from Tetherite Ore in a blast furnace (a furnace will not take it). A slain Cragback drops some, and the Fray's tangles hold a little.
Deep in the hearts of the Seam's islands and in the stone of the Fray's knots. Only a netherite pickaxe brings it out.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.seam_vein: Glowing veins in the stone of the Seam. Broken, they give Seam Silk, and they count for the veins Rift Trial.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.veil_wing: Left by Veil Rays over the Seam, and by Frayed Rays and the Knot Mother; now and then in a barrel of the Thinned. Woven into a Mending Cloth.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.blood_cord: Sold by a Hollowling once the tribe trusts you. Use it on another player to bind the two of you into a clan.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.mending_th: Lies at the Heart of the Seam once the Starved One is slain, beside the Severing Shears. Use it to mend the first wound; only one of the two can ever be used.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.severing_s: Lie at the Heart of the Seam once the Starved One is slain, beside the Mending Thread. Use them to sever the Tether; only one of the two can ever be used.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.echo_threa: One of the First Weaver's four threads, left in the frame of an Ancient City. Twist all four round an iron chain to make a Plumb Line.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.ember_thre: One of the First Weaver's four threads, tied round a ledger of gold in piglin script in the Nether. Twist all four round an iron chain to make a Plumb Line.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.pale_threa: One of the First Weaver's four threads, in an empty socket ringed with end stone in the End. Twist all four round an iron chain to make a Plumb Line.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.silk_threa: One of the First Weaver's four threads, pulled from a half-woven tapestry in the Seam. Twist all four round an iron chain to make a Plumb Line.

viewer.extremedimensions.info.music_disc: Now and then in a barrel of the Thinned in the Seam; the richer the barrel, the likelier.
In the Fray's tangles and in the tribe's hoards.
Left by a slain Cave or Sculk Lurker, and found in Ancient City chests.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.disc_fragm: Each Elder leaves two to everyone who fought it. Nine make Elegy of the Elders.
An Abyssal curse leaves one as it breaks; very rarely a tangle in the Fray or a Frayed Ray does. Nine make The Abyss Answers.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.helds_chai: A relic that lies in the Held's chamber at the end of a warm chain; Keepers, the Seam's chests and the Starved One may hold one too. Bind it to your Tether for its gift, and bear its price.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.relic: A relic: found with Keepers, in the Seam's chests and with the Starved One, and the Elders leave them; kin may barter for one. Bind it to your Tether, one at a time, for its gift, and bear its price. Each serves once: it stays bound until another takes its place, and then it crumbles. Each is common, uncommon, rare or epic: the rarer, the more rarely found, and great foes leave the rarer ones more often.
viewer.extremedimensions.info.relic_kept: A relic: found with Keepers, in the Seam's chests and with the Starved One, and the Elders leave them; kin may barter for one. viewer.extremedimensions.info.lodestone: Within 5 blocks of a Nether or an End portal and fed that world's fuel, a lodestone becomes an anchor: it stores time beyond the wound for you. Bind your Tether to it before you step through.

journal.extremedimensions.matriarch.text: Kill enough of her children's keepers and she comes herself. Taller than any Keeper, her mask cracked with age, her cloak the colour of old blood. She calls her brood to take what they can while she fights, and when she wails the light goes out of the world for a while. She is the oldest thing in the hollows. Perhaps the first one who stayed.
journal.extremedimensions.ferryman.title: 33. The Ferryman
journal.extremedimensions.ferryman.text: So that is who the pigmen pay. He never walked before the dragon fell: the crack it left in the world let him through. He comes for those who stay too long beyond the wound, poling his way through the heat to the toll of a single bell. While he walks, the thread drains as if it were paying him. Every blow costs you levels. Go home with him still walking and he takes his fare anyway. Stand and fight, and he forgets what you owe.
journal.extremedimensions.last_weaver.te: Not all of them finished weaving themselves into the seal. One may wait in any village of the Thinned, half thread and half person, keeping what is left of its people. With the hunger at the Heart ended, they are waking. Its touch unpicks the thread that holds you in the Seam. End it, and the thread it was keeping is yours.

journal.extremedimensions.barter.title: 35. Small Bargains
journal.extremedimensions.barter.text: They remember. Every nugget I left by a hoard, every Hollowling I let run, every one I did not. Today one of them did not freeze when I looked at it. It came closer, held out a fragment of the Tether in its grey little hands, and waited. It wanted gold. Not much. A few nuggets, a shard of amethyst, things that shine. It gives what it finds, and it finds what we lose. I think the tribe is keeping count of me. I think I would like to be worth something to it.
journal.extremedimensions.raid.title: 36. The Raid
journal.extremedimensions.raid.text: It was not my hoard. I opened it anyway. They came out of the ground like ink out of a broken bottle, all of them at once, giggling, grabbing at everything I carried, and they did not freeze when I looked at them. Then the Keeper. When it fell the barrel was fuller than any I had seen: fragments, pages, emeralds, things the tribe had hidden away for a very long time. I took it all. Somewhere in the dark, someone is keeping count.

journal.extremedimensions.fray.title: 37. The Fray
journal.extremedimensions.fray.text: There is a well at the edge of some islands, a ring of stone around nothing. I dropped a lantern into one and watched it fall until the fog took it. Then I jumped. The Seam caught me, the way it catches dust, and let me down onto a knot of thread as big as a house, wound round stone, far below the islands. Strands run from knot to knot into the dark. Everything the Seam swallows ends up tangled here. My time ran through my fingers twice as fast, and the Thinned did not wait for me to grow weak. I crouched on the knot's glowing heart and the updraft carried me home.
journal.extremedimensions.frayed_ray.tex: The rays came down after me. I had thought them the gentlest things in the Seam, but these were not the rays I knew: their light had turned the green of a bruise going bad, and their eyes were coals. One cried out, climbed, folded its wings and fell on me like a stone. Its sting burned for a long while after. I think the Fray does to them what it does to everything that sinks into it. I did not stay to see what it would do to me.
journal.extremedimensions.held.title: 39. The Held
journal.extremedimensions.held.text: If you are reading this, you followed the chain. The other one never did. They stood at the gate with a hand on the warm links, wrote something in that little book, and walked away. I heard the footsteps go. I have held this chain since before the wounds had names. Not against anything. For someone. When the door was cut, someone had to keep it from swinging shut on those still on the other side, and a chain was all there was. My hands are bone now. They still know how to hold. Take it. It will hold you as it held me: a little longer than it should, and never long enough. And when you read that book again, read it in my hand as well. Whoever wrote it was not the first. Nobody who says so ever is.
journal.extremedimensions.echoes.title: 40. Echoes
journal.extremedimensions.echoes.text: Where one of us was dragged out, the place does not forget. I went back, once, to where a friend's thread ran dry. She was still there, kneeling, the chains held up as if someone would come for her. I stood by her until she let go. It cost me time I did not have. She left me something, and I think she left something for herself as well, wherever she was. The wound remembers us. I do not know yet whether that is a mercy.
journal.extremedimensions.frame.title: 41. The Frame
journal.extremedimensions.frame.text: Not empty. Unstrung. Put silk across it and it remembers: they came out of the dark one after another and stepped into the weave, and the weave closed behind them. The first of them did not step in. The first of them was tying something. Look for the rest where the piglins keep their gold, where the cities of the End keep theirs, and on the looms in the Seam where nobody weaves any more. Then go down. The thread runs deeper than the Wanderer ever went.
journal.extremedimensions.first_knot.tex: A knot the size of a hall, and the strands of the whole Seam running into it. It was tied, not grown. Something is tied into it as well, at its heart, and it is not asleep. The Wanderer wrote that they were the first. The Weavers say nothing; they are woven. I say this: whoever tied this knot is still holding the end of it.
journal.extremedimensions.deep.title: 43. What Listens
journal.extremedimensions.deep.text: Down where the torches give out lives one of them that does not watch. It has no use for watching. It listens. I heard it before I saw it: a dry clicking in the dark that quickened every time my pick struck stone. When I stopped, it stopped. I learned to walk the deep places softly, like a thief in my own tunnels. The one time I forgot, it came out of the black on all fours and laid its hand on me, and I carry what it left me still. Its kin take. This one only marks. Walk softly, and if the clicking quickens, raise your shield.
journal.extremedimensions.herald.title: 44. The Warden's Herald
journal.extremedimensions.herald.text: Under the deep dark there are cities older than ours, and the stone there grows a skin that hears. Some of the tribe went down that far and found a new master. I met one: small, wrapped in sculk, its mask the colour of old bone. It never touched me. It scratched at the shriekers instead, patient as a bell-ringer, until something vast stirred under my feet. Then it went to the thing and led it to me, clicking all the way, and the thing would not touch it. And all the while it laughed, low and wet like water in a throat: when it set the listening stones clicking in my name, when it caught me looking at it, and last of all from a safe way off, as the thing came for me. Kill the little one before it rings. Or do not go down at all.
journal.extremedimensions.continued_mend: The Wanderer's ink stops where mine starts. The wound is shut, and the world is already forgetting it was ever open: the storms do not come, the young of the tribe leave things on the doorstep, and the drain is a whisper where it was a pull. But a seam is never gone, only sewn. I have built a loom from the Weavers' own pillars, and I mean to weave down what we did, deed by deed, before the world forgets that too. Six panels. When the last is set, I think the wounds will remember us one last time, all at once. Let them. I will be at the loom.
journal.extremedimensions.continued_seve: The Wanderer's ink stops where mine starts. The Tether is cut, and the seconds no longer run out beyond the wound. Nothing calls us home now, and nothing will catch us if we fall: whoever falls there keeps nothing. I have built a loom from the Weavers' own pillars, because a world with no thread to hold it needs something woven instead. What we did, deed by deed, so that it is kept somewhere. Six panels. When the last is set, I think the wounds will come for the loom, all at once. Let them. I will be at the loom.
journal.extremedimensions.note.ruined_ga: Still warm. You looked longer than they did.
journal.extremedimensions.note.wanderer: First? I tied my cord before you were born.
journal.extremedimensions.note.first_wou: A door. Yes. Ask who held it open.
journal.extremedimensions.note.unanchore: They finish only when no one is looking. I looked, for a hundred years.

gui.extremedimensions.path.title: The Path
gui.extremedimensions.path.seam.craft: Craft a Seam Needle from 2 Tether Fragments, an unread Wanderer's Page and an Echo Shard. Monsters slain beyond the wound drop fragments; pages lie in chests at ruined portals, fortresses and strongholds; Echo Shards in the Ancient Cities.
gui.extremedimensions.path.seam.tear: Use the Seam Needle on Crying Obsidian, in the Overworld or the Nether, with room in front of it, and walk into the tear before it closes. Crying Obsidian lies at ruined portals; piglins trade it.
gui.extremedimensions.path.seam_home: The gate you stepped out of is the way home: walk back into the rift between its pylons before your time runs out. Lost sight of it? Follow the arrow on your bar.
gui.extremedimensions.path.seal: The Ender Dragon is the lock on the first wound. Once it falls, every rift into the Seam opens at its Heart until the world is chosen: finish what you still seek in the Seam first. Ready a Void Anchor with plenty of charge: the End lies beyond the wound too.
gui.extremedimensions.path.heart: Since the seal broke, every rift into the Seam opens at its Heart. Tear one with a Seam Needle; what waits there came through the first wound.
gui.extremedimensions.path.starved: The Starved One waits at the Heart. It flies, calls the tribe's red young and turns the Veil Rays on you, and free it takes only part of the harm. Strands run from the Heart to four great pillars, and high up each (on top of the lowest piece of its shaft) a glowing heart of sculk heals it through a beam of souls. Quench three (an arrow does it, or breaking it, or Seam Silk) and it heals no more; all four and it falls stunned, taking double damage. A bow is the key. A Hollowling at your side makes it easier, and your thread does not run at the Heart while it lives.
gui.extremedimensions.path.choose: The Mending Thread and the Severing Shears lie at the altar of the Heart. Only one of the two can ever be used, and it decides for the whole world.
gui.extremedimensions.path.choose.held: You carry what decides the world. The Thread mends the first wound: the world grows calm and the tribe makes peace. The Shears sever the Tether: no time runs out beyond the wound, but who falls there keeps nothing. Only one can ever be used.
gui.extremedimensions.path.beyond: The Wanderer's path ends here; the world is not finished. Weave six threads on a Weaver's Loom: the Matriarch, the Ferryman, the Last Weaver (now in the villages of the Thinned), the Held, the Knot Mother and the Heart. The sixth begins the Weaving: hold the loom. Pacts are open now.
gui.extremedimensions.ending.unfinished: The story is chosen; the world is not finished. Six threads wait on a Weaver's Loom: the Matriarch's, the Ferryman's, the Last Weaver's, the Held's, the Knot Mother's and the Heart's. When the last is set, the Weaving begins.
gui.extremedimensions.path.finished: The tapestry is finished, and the story is yours. New Thread+ on the loom sets the whole world a harder thread, and the Rift Trials and the Unweaving are still there for you.

gui.extremedimensions.frame.shows: The strung frame remembers what it held...

gui.extremedimensions.tapestry.new_threa: %s takes up a new thread. Thread %s: the Elders are stronger, atonement dearer, and the trials have no end.
gui.extremedimensions.weaving.begins: The last panel is set. The wounds converge on the loom: hold it until the weave is done!
gui.extremedimensions.weaving.held: The weave holds. The tapestry is finished, and the story is yours.

gui.extremedimensions.first_knot.reached: The First Knot. Something is tied into its heart.
gui.extremedimensions.first_knot.resting: The knot is pulled tight. What was tied into it has not come back yet.
gui.extremedimensions.plumb.down: The line pulls down, and %s, %s blocks off. Find a well to the Fray.
gui.extremedimensions.plumb.here: The line hangs straight: you are at the knot.
gui.extremedimensions.plumb.tear: The line pulls %s, %s blocks off: tear your rift there, and the Knot hangs below where you land.
gui.extremedimensions.plumb.tear_here: The line hangs straight: tear your rift here, and the Knot hangs below where you land.
gui.extremedimensions.plumb.heart: The line hangs still: while the seal is broken, every rift opens at the Heart.
gui.extremedimensions.loom.new: A loom just set down holds nothing of theirs. The thread is on the Weavers' own looms.
gui.extremedimensions.heart.offers_again: The altar gives up the Thread and the Shears again: the world's ending is still yours to choose.
gui.extremedimensions.heart.still: The altar is still: what came through the first wound is gone for good. The Mending Thread and the Severing Shears decide now; until one is used, every rift opens here.
gui.extremedimensions.heart.socket_gone: The pillar stays dark: what it held down is gone for good.
gui.extremedimensions.heart.socket_wait: The pillar stays dark: it answers only while the Starved One stands. Step onto the altar to wake it.
gui.extremedimensions.heart.awake: The Starved One rises, and the four great pillars round the Heart feed it: high up each, on top of the lowest piece of its shaft, a glowing heart of sculk heals it through a beam of souls. Quench them: shoot one with an arrow (or throw anything at it), break it, or feed it %2$s Seam Silk. With %1$s quenched it heals no more; with all %3$s it falls stunned. Free, it takes only part of the harm.
gui.extremedimensions.heart.socket_fed: The pillar's heart drinks the silk (%s of %s).
gui.extremedimensions.heart.socket_lit: A pillar is quenched: %s of %s. With %s quenched it heals no more.
gui.extremedimensions.heart.socket_burni: This pillar is quenched already (%s s left).
gui.extremedimensions.heart.socket_dark: A pillar wakes and feeds the Starved One again (%s still quenched).
gui.extremedimensions.heart.bound: Every pillar is quenched: the Starved One falls stunned! Strike now.
gui.extremedimensions.heart.unbound: The Starved One shakes off the stun. The pillars still quenched stay so for their time.
gui.extremedimensions.seam.toll: The Seam keeps its share as it throws you out: %s Seam Silk and %s Tether Fragments.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.collapse.text: Your charge ran out and the Tether pulled you down. A curse follows you home: you choose which, from the cards.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.curse.title: Curses
gui.extremedimensions.hint.curse.text: A curse stays until lifted: by atonement earned beyond the wound, helped along by Tether Fragments offered at an anchor. See them under Curses in your inventory.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.fragment.text: Offer fragments at an anchor: each atones for a tenth of what your curse still asks (much at first, little later), five at most for each stack. Two, a Wanderer's Page and an Echo Shard make a Seam Needle.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.lurker.title: The Lurker
gui.extremedimensions.hint.lurker.text: It stalks what does not look at it. A blue glow means it came to steal, red that it came to hurt; struck, it may turn on you.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.hoard.title: A hoard
gui.extremedimensions.hint.hoard.text: What the tribe steals ends up here. Take it back, but opening it wakes its Keeper.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.relic.title: A relic
gui.extremedimensions.hint.relic.text: Use it at home to bind it to your Tether. Each gives and each takes, and each serves once: it stays bound until another takes its place, and then it crumbles.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.relic.text_ke: Use it at home to bind it to your Tether. Each gives and each takes; a bound relic is never lost.
gui.extremedimensions.choice.forced: No choice. The abyss chose for you.
gui.extremedimensions.abyssal.broken: %1$s breaks. It no longer holds you.
gui.extremedimensions.abyssal.cloth: The cloth will not take %s. Break it, or atone.
gui.extremedimensions.abyssal.hungering: The Starved took %s × %s from your bag.
gui.extremedimensions.abyssal.gravebound: You wake where it all began.
gui.extremedimensions.abyssal.lockjaw: Your jaw will not open with them this close.
gui.extremedimensions.abyssal.blood_jump: The blood price: the stack leaps onto %s.
gui.extremedimensions.abyssal.lightless_: You slept. The nights you kept are forgotten.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.abyssal.title: An abyssal curse
gui.extremedimensions.hint.abyssal.text: No cloth and no friend takes it from you. Its deed breaks it: read it under Curses, in the Extreme tab.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.unweaving.tex: One of your curse sets is full. At the world's Weaver's Loom, Tetherite and Tether Cords can unweave it, if you cut its knots in time.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.portal.title: A wound in the world
gui.extremedimensions.hint.portal.text: It opens only for one who is bound. Set a lodestone within five blocks of it, feed it fuel, and bind a Tether to it.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.lodestone.tex: Set it beside a portal and feed it. Coal or blaze powder by a Nether portal makes an Ember Anchor; amethyst or ender pearls by an End portal, a Void Anchor.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.wound.title: The wound stays shut
gui.extremedimensions.hint.wound.text: It opens only for one bound to an anchor beside it. The Path in the Tether Journal shows what is still missing.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.end_portal.te: An anchor holds here too: a lodestone within five blocks of this portal, fed with amethyst, chorus fruit or ender pearls, becomes a Void Anchor. Beyond it the dragon is the lock: once it falls, every rift into the Seam opens at its Heart until the world is chosen.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.needle.title: Seam Needle
gui.extremedimensions.hint.needle.text: Use it on Crying Obsidian in the Overworld or the Nether, then walk into the tear. The gate you arrive at leads home.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.silk.title: Seam Silk
gui.extremedimensions.hint.silk.text: It weaves stronger Tethers and cheaper Seam Needles. The recipe book shows what it makes.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.elder.title: An Elder
gui.extremedimensions.hint.elder.text: Nothing can hurt it while it forms. Use these seconds to choose your ground.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.storm.title: A Wound Storm
gui.extremedimensions.hint.storm.text: Things slip through behind you. Fight with your back to a wall; the storm stops when you leave the Overworld.
gui.extremedimensions.hint.fallen.title: Fallen
gui.extremedimensions.hint.fallen.text: An ally who crouches beside you for 4 seconds lifts you up. Hold sneak for 3 seconds to give in.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.unseen_te: The page is blank. Whatever belongs here, you have not met it yet.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.notes_loc: Slay %s more to learn how to face it.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.noted: Your journal now knows how to face %s.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.lurker.lo: Tall, thin and grey as smoke, it stands where the light gives out and watches. It wants what you carry: your things, your memories, the light in your anchors. Look away and it is closer.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.lurker.no: Soul light keeps it from your anchors. Once it has taken something it flees: catch it before it vanishes and it drops what it took.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.cave_lurk: Pale, damp and low enough for a miner's tunnel, it lives in the deepest caves. It has little use for eyes: it listens.
Sneak, and it hears nothing. Its clicks quicken as it hears more, and rattle when it comes. Its grab always curses: a shield turns it aside.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.sculk_lur: Small and quiet as the sculk it walks on, it serves what sleeps under the Ancient Cities. It never strikes you.
It rattles the shriekers to wake the Warden, then leads it to you. The Warden spares it: kill it before it calls.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.magpie.lo: A lean thief of the tribe, black-cloaked and white-masked, with a glint of gold in its eyes. It never touches you. It goes for what you keep, and runs it home with the brightest piece held high.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.magpie.no: It robs chests and barrels left alone near you, the brightest things first. Every blow shakes one thing loose; slain, it drops it all. Follow it, and you find the hoard where it keeps the rest.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.wick.lore: A knee-high thing of tallow and soot with a flame for eyes. On dark nights it comes to where the light is, and eats it.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.wick.note: It eats torches and lanterns and snuffs out candles until it is full. Soul fire frightens it and water puts it out. Slain, it gives back what it ate; full, it bursts into flame, so keep your distance.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.tidewalke: Kin of the tribe gone down into the deep water, its cloak turned to kelp and its mask grown over with barnacles. It lies just under the surface where someone rows or swims.

A trail of bubbles is all you see before it strikes: it throws you out of your boat, or drags you under and tears the breath out of you. A blow makes it let go. A torch or lantern held up, or the Conduit's power, keeps it off; it never follows you ashore.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.gatebreak: The biggest of the tribe, a slow giant of storm-grey stone and iron that the Wound Storms wake. It steps out of a tear in the storm for whoever the storm rages round.

Walls do not stop it: it breaks through stone and wood alike, though obsidian holds. Stay out of reach of its slam, or raise a shield as its fists come down. Fight it together: it grows stronger with every player near, and it goes when the storm passes.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.lockwarde: The Dragon was the lock on the first wound, and this one of the tribe kept watch over the lock. With the Dragon fallen there is no lock left to keep, and it roams the End after what still opens ways.

It comes only for those who carry ender pearls, stepping closer as an Enderman does, and snatches them; sometimes it leaves you on a lost islet with one pearl to get back. A raised shield turns its reach. Strike it and half of what it took falls; slay it and all of it does.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.threadbit: The Seam keeps its own small ones: scraps of the tribe that never left, grown mouths too big for them on the thread that holds visitors in. They run in packs, and their cloaks glint with the gold they have eaten.

A pack comes for visitors to the Seam, more often once their thread runs thin. Each bite takes a few seconds of your time (never all of it); after a few bites it runs off, trailing gold. Slay it before it is gone and every second it ate comes back.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.edgecrawl: Under the islands of the Seam, where no one looks, something clings to the stone. It is grey as the undersides it lives on, long in the arm, and its mask is set with small glowing eyes. It knows the islands end, and it knows who forgets.

It comes only for those who stand near an edge, climbing up over the rim behind them, and moves only while it is not looked at. It grabs and drags you to the edge to throw you over: crouch to plant your feet, raise a shield against its reach, or strike it to make it let go. With no edge near, it claws.
Some of the tribe lay down in the Seam so long ago that the islands grew over them. Their backs are stone now, veined with Tetherite, and they sleep where they lay. They do not like to be dug at.

Asleep it is a boulder like any other. Break blocks near it (Tetherite ore from further off), strike it, or stand by it without crouching and it wakes: a slam that throws you back, and rocks that fall where a ring of dust shows. A shield turns the slam. Slain, it gives up the Tetherite of its back.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.hollowlin: The young of the tribe: small, quick and giggling. They freeze when you look at them, steal small things when you don't, and carry them home to their hoard.
They never take tools, armour or anything of the Tether. Small shiny gifts win the tribe over; a Tether Fragment in soul light may win a companion. Killing them costs dearly.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.keeper.lo: The guardian of a hoard: a Lurker grown huge and patient. Open what it keeps, or hurt its young, and it comes for you, screeching darkness.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.keeper.no: It blinks behind you when you run and its screech slows you: keep it in sight and fight close. Go far enough from its hoard and it gives up.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.starved_o: What came through the first wound, and what the tribe has hidden from ever since. Not a Weaver but the hunger itself: a starved, hooded thing some six blocks tall with no face but a maw of embers, its ribs open on an empty belly of fire, a crown of broken iron on its brow and the snapped chains of a binding that could not hold it. It hangs in the air and drinks time itself.

It grows stronger for every player at the Heart, heals from the four pillars until three of their hearts are quenched, and free it shrugs off much of the harm. Bring a bow and arrows for the pillars' hearts and for when it circles, and patience.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.thinned.l: What is left of the Weavers' people, worn to threads, still walking the streets of their villages in the Seam. They mean nothing by their watching, until your thread runs thin.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.thinned.n: They only move while nobody looks at them: keep them in sight and back away. In the Fray they hunt from the start. They carry Seam Silk.
Great pale rays that glide high over the islands of the Seam, trailing light. They circle every visitor, curious, and mean no harm.
Brought down, they give Seam Silk, glow ink and their wings. A Veil Wing mends what the Seam unravels.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.frayed_ra: Veil Rays that sank into the Fray and came back wrong. Their light has gone sick and green, their eyes red. They fly faster than their kin above, climb over whoever comes down, fold their wings and dive.

Listen for the cry: it comes before the climb. Step aside as it folds its wings, or strike it as it pulls away. Its sting poisons. When the dark closes in, they all come at once. They carry more silk than the rays above.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.matriarch: The mother of the hollows: a weeping mask of carved wood on a body of roots and bark, tall as a tree. She guards her hoards herself once too many Keepers have fallen.
Watch the ground: every blow is foretold by her sigil. Jump her rings. Her brood steals while she fights, so guard your pockets.
The ferryman of the Nether's last river: hooded, with a skull beneath and soul fire in its sockets. He asks a toll of every soul that crosses, and takes it whether you pay or not.
Every blow he lands takes its toll. His chains pull you in and his cage crushes inward: break his line of sight and keep moving.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.weaver.lo: The last of the Weavers who sewed the Seam shut. Gowned in silk and light, a gem for an eye, she unpicks what visitors weave, and the time they carry.
gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.weaver.no: Her threads pull taut before they cut: step off the line. Her blows take Seam time. The Seraphic Lance is foretold by a line of light on the ground: get out of its path.
gui.extremedimensions.ledger.page.close: Every number here is a night I lived through.

gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.knot_moth: What is tied into the First Knot, deep in the Fray. Where the Last Weaver unmakes the thread, she binds it. A tall veiled figure in robes of charcoal and violet, a hood full of dark with a crack of light where a face would be, a crown of bronze thorns behind her head and rings that float about her; at her breast a core of violet light in a frame of thorns, and from her clawed fingers threads of amber. Whether she is the First Weaver, what the Fray made of her, or someone else, the journal does not say.

She ties herself to three anchors round her chamber, pillars of crying obsidian with a node of amber light, and while they stand she shrugs off half of every blow. Break a node (three hits) and she is exposed: she hangs still, her core open, and blows bite deeper. At 70% and 35% she ties them all again. Her Threadline sweeps a thread low across the floor: jump it, or step out of its lane. Her Knot Snare draws closing patterns on the floor: get out before they close or be held fast and lose Seam time. Her light warns you: amber for the Threadline, violet for the Snare, white when she lies exposed.

gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.pale_haul: The Endermen of the far islands were people once, and they are building their way home. The Haulers fetch the stone, and they like best the stone someone laid out over the void.

They come in twos and threes in the Pale Reach. A block shakes in a Hauler's grip before it comes loose; look the Hauler in the eye and it lets go and steps away, and the third time it goes. Never a block you stand on or beside: the gap opens a step ahead. With nothing to haul it crouches, then leaps. Slay it and every block it took falls.

journal.extremedimensions.pale_reach.tex: Far out past the last of the cities the islands thin to nothing, and there they build. Half an anchor hangs over the void, golden posts round an empty socket, a ring of stone not yet closed. No Enderman finishes one. They fetch stone from everywhere, and they fetch it from under your feet if you lay a path to them. Give the socket an eye of the End and it steadies the Tether near it, as if it remembered what it was meant for. The wind out there is not wind. It is the void breathing in.

gui.extremedimensions.bestiary.pale_maso: The foreman of the Endermen of the Pale Reach, the first of them torn loose when the wound opened, and the one who keeps them building. Eighteen blocks of Enderman under a hood and mantle of pale stone, chains of gold, a broken halo. He wants the one thing his anchor lacks: a Tether.

He blinks to your side and brings a claw down where a sigil burns: step off it. His walls hem you in, but shelter you from his Door. Watch the shadows of the blocks he lifts. When his eyes blaze, do not look him in the face (a carved pumpkin keeps his gaze off). At his Door, sneak and keep a wall at your back. When cubes of light swing round him on their chains, stand inside the ring on the floor or outside it. Step off the sigils of his pillars, jump his golden rings, and when the floor winds up round him, brace against a wall and be far away when it bursts.
journal.extremedimensions.pale_mason.tex: They have a master out there, and he is the worst of them, because he remembers best. He was the first to be torn loose. He does not fetch stone; he is stone, piled up in the shape of a man too tall for any door, and he has been building the same door since before the cities. He knows what it lacks. He looked at my Tether the way a mason looks at the last stone. He goes from here to there without crossing between. Do not look at his face. If he opens his door, put a wall between you and it, and pray the wall holds.

journal.extremedimensions.last_stone.tex: If anyone ever brings the Mason down, look at what he leaves. He carries two things against his chest and never sets either down: the last stone of their door, and the lock for it. I think he could never decide either. Set the stone in a fitting they have woken, and their anchor closes, and they walk home through it, all of them, and the End is quiet after. Set the lock instead, and the door is shut for good, and everything they put by for the way home is yours, and they will never forgive it. Only one of the two can be set. I would set the stone. I am not sure I would.
